title: Unravelling mutation patterns in Extended-Spectrum beta-Lactamases for precision drug design against AMR in Enterobacteriaceae.
one_liner_zh: 该文分析ESBL基因突变模式与转录因子结合位点，但核心是抗菌素耐药性药物设计，非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，且无AI/物理模拟方法，仅间接提及机器学习数据集。
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) presents a critical global challenge, causing over 1.27 million deaths annually, with projections reaching 10 million by 2050. Among the most concerning contributors are Enterobacteriaceae, particularly Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, which harbour Extended-Spectrum beta-Lactamase (ESBL) genes-enzymes that hydrolyse beta-lactam antibiotics and confer resistance-such as bla-CTX-M, bla-SHV, and bla-TEM. These genes confer resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics, including penicillins and cephalosporins, limiting treatment options for urinary tract infections, bloodstream infections, and pneumonia. The World Health Organisation has classified these pathogens as critical targets for new drug development. In this study, we comprehensively analysed all known variants of bla-CTX-M, bla-SHV, and bla-TEM genes along with their wild-type sequences. Using a multi-step computational approach, we assessed guanine-cytosine (GC) content, single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs; single-base changes in DNA), insertion and deletion (InDel) variants (mutations involving nucleotide addition or removal), codon usage patterns, transcription factor binding sites (TFBS; DNA regions regulating gene expression), amino acid composition, protein stability, mutational hotspots, nucleotide and amino acid mutation frequencies, hydrophobicity, isoelectric point, aromaticity, aliphatic index, and molecular flexibility. The integrated dataset maps conserved regions and identifies residues frequently associated with resistance phenotypes. Our findings provide a framework for predicting resistance-associated mutation patterns and identifying genomic regions suitable for resistance-free drug targeting. These insights support prioritising drug target sites, optimising screening libraries, and generating high-quality datasets for machine learning-based precision drug design.
abstract_zh: 抗菌药物耐药性（AMR）构成一项严峻的全球性挑战，每年导致超过127万人死亡，预计到2050年这一数字将达到1000万。其中，最令人担忧的贡献者之一是肠杆菌科（Enterobacteriaceae），尤其是大肠杆菌（Escherichia coli）和肺炎克雷伯菌（Klebsiella pneumoniae），它们携带超广谱β-内酰胺酶（ESBL）基因——这些酶能水解β-内酰胺类抗生素并赋予耐药性——例如bla-CTX-M、bla-SHV和bla-TEM。这些基因赋予对β-内酰胺类抗生素（包括青霉素类和头孢菌素类）的耐药性，从而限制了尿路感染、血流感染和肺炎的治疗选择。世界卫生组织已将这些病原体列为新药开发的优先关键目标。在本研究中，我们全面分析了bla-CTX-M、bla-SHV和bla-TEM基因的所有已知变体及其野生型序列。采用多步骤计算方法，我们评估了鸟嘌呤-胞嘧啶（GC）含量、单核苷酸多态性（SNPs；DNA中的单碱基变化）、插入和缺失（InDel）变体（涉及核苷酸添加或移除的突变）、密码子使用模式、转录因子结合位点（TFBS；调控基因表达的DNA区域）、氨基酸组成、蛋白质稳定性、突变热点、核苷酸和氨基酸突变频率、疏水性、等电点、芳香性、脂肪族指数和分子柔性。整合的数据集绘制了保守区域图谱，并识别出与耐药表型频繁相关的残基。我们的发现为预测耐药相关突变模式和识别适合无耐药性药物靶向的基因组区域提供了框架。这些见解支持优先确定药物靶点位点、优化筛选文库，并为基于机器学习的精准药物设计生成高质量数据集。
